A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OmniTalker, with matching architecture, baselines and substantial shared results. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable throughout. v1 ends with references; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original speech and video generation experiments, fusion ablations and qualitative motion analyses in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, fusion ablations, a 50-participant user study and additional gaze and emotional-generation examples, including appendix results.

M1.justification: The dual-branch DiT, joint attention, reference conditioning and decoders remain. Localized procedural revisions include stated L1 rather than squared-error training, logit-normal rather than uniform timestep sampling, and condition-specific guidance replacing generic scalar CFG. v2 also describes multiple masked segments instead of v1's reference/target pair. Newly documented renderer details alone do not establish a new renderer.

E1.justification: Reported evaluation coverage changes from v1's pooled VFHQ, MEAD and real-world collection to separate SEED speech, VoxCeleb2 video and Chinese Custom evaluations. Appendix B.3 adds RAVDESS emotional-reference examples. Several SEED speech columns reproduce earlier scores, so their new dataset label alone should not be mistaken for new experimental coverage.

E2.justification: The external TTS and talking-head baseline sets remain unchanged. However, v2 Table 4 adds Cross-Attention alongside Add and Linear as an evaluated comparator in the fusion experiment corresponding to v1 Table 3.

E3.justification: v1 describes 1,000 pooled test samples; v2 specifies 500 VoxCeleb2 clips and 100 Custom clips. AniTalker's reported evaluation resolution changes from 256×256 to 512×512 with super-resolution. PSNR, SSIM and image FID are dropped. A new user-study protocol uses 50 references, 50 participants and six dimensions rated from 1 to 5. These are reported protocol changes, not proof that all retained results were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond extending the fusion ablation with Cross-Attention, v2 adds substantial qualitative investigation of gaze dynamics, coordination with head motion and reference-eye-style inheritance in Figures 7–9, plus emotional-reference transfer in Figure 10. The earlier yaw trajectories and motion heatmaps are retained rather than newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bars for the experimental results. The new user study reports mean ratings without uncertainty estimates; participant counts are evaluation-design information.

E6.justification: v2 adds VoxCeleb2, Custom-speech, MOS and Cross-Attention results, while removing PSNR/SSIM/FID entries and the earlier fully conditioned ZH/EN speech scores. In the largely retained video-results block, Sync-C changes from 0.597 to 4.17 for StyleTalk, 6.548 to 5.52 for Hallo, and 5.354 to 5.48 for OmniTalker. Changed test-set descriptions prevent treating these as established same-setting gains. Reported renderer speed changes from 30 to 50 FPS, while overall generation remains 25 FPS.

T1.justification: v2 adds explicit landmark-fitting and renderer-loss formulations and revises the mathematical formulation of CFG to use condition-specific weights. Appendix A.1 expands the conditional-flow derivation with marginalization identities, while retaining its underlying OT objective. No new theorem or proved guarantee is introduced.

C1.justification: Joint generation, multimodal style replication and 25-FPS inference remain the central claims. v2 additionally foregrounds novelty as the first unified one-shot text-to-audio-video framework and no longer lists the data pipeline and multistage training as a separate principal contribution. The zero-shot/one-shot terminology change does not establish a different reference-conditioning task.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning head-only generation and GAN artifacts under large motion, explanations of gaze–head coordination and text-conditioning design, and clarification that baseline FPS excludes preceding TTS. Existing multitask-learning and frontal-view metric-bias interpretations remain. These additions qualify and explain the retained conclusions rather than replacing them.

D1.justification: v2 supplies extensive previously absent implementation information: training on eight A100s for 750,000 iterations, batch size and learning rate, feature extraction and temporal alignment, masking/dropout rates, CFG settings, sampling steps, renderer losses, preprocessing thresholds and model configurations. These disclosures substantially improve reproducibility, although prose specifying 512-dimensional audio/visual embeddings conflicts with Table 5's 1024-dimensional entries.

R1.justification: The main research positioning and closest competing approaches remain. v2 adds an explicit distinction from MMAudio's separate text branch and references such as StyleTalk++, MimicTalk and LivePortrait, alongside dataset and preprocessing sources. The earlier NeRF/Gaussian-splatting discussion and ChatAnyone citation are removed. This updates supporting context without fundamentally changing the research position.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much related-work prose are rewritten. Method subsections are reorganized around alignment, fusion, generation and decoding; experimental setup is consolidated and qualitative evaluation separated. Flow-matching background moves into an appendix, alongside newly organized technical, experimental, limitations and impact sections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. The introductory pipeline illustration disappears, and the architecture diagram is redrawn to show four fusion variants. Benchmark tables gain dataset groupings, while MOS and configuration tables and several appendix figures are added. The original yaw plot and qualitative heatmap comparison are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's sparse reproducibility documentation through Appendices A–B and adds human evaluation and gaze/emotion analyses directly relevant to its central style-replication claim. Specific failure conditions also improve assessability. These gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses, including ambiguous provenance of reused scores, inconsistent embedding dimensions, overbroad metric-superiority wording and absent uncertainty estimates.
